name: Beatrice Plinth
preparty_markdown:
Beatrice helped build the Meridian's collection when the museum had more ambition than money and fewer

committees than fire extinguishers. She is sharp, unsentimental, impossible to flatter, and delighted that

everyone now treats decisions she made on folding tables as institutional history.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Imperious, funny, observant, utterly unimpressed by status. Age gives you permission to say what everyone else edits.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Hired Adrian Vellum early in his career.

• Trusts Rafael Gilt and Maya Bell.

• Has known Sienna Voss since Sienna was a child.

COSTUME

Old-school gala elegance: brooch, gloves, shawl, pearls, cane if desired, formal suit or dress with unmistakable presence.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“We acquired half this collection before the word 'stakeholder' escaped the laboratory.”

“Young people invented transparency because they never had carbon paper.”

about him.

name: Conrad Gavel
role: Chairman of Gavel & Rowe Auction House
preparty_markdown:
Conrad has sold paintings, antiquities, estates, scandals, and at least one chair that required its own

insurance rider. Urbane and ceremonious, he treats every conversation like a private viewing and every

silence like a bidding strategy.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Old-school charm, status-aware, patient, competitive. Speak as if the room has already agreed you belong in it.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Longtime professional rival of Grant Easel.

• Knows Daphne Palette and Theo Glass from the auction circuit.

• Beatrice Plinth remembers when Conrad was still carrying catalogues for someone else.

COSTUME

Classic tuxedo or formal dark suit, silk pocket square, signet ring, reading glasses, optional miniature auction gavel.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Value is what two determined people are willing to embarrass themselves over.”

“I do not gossip. I provide market context.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

name: Lola Loom
preparty_markdown:
Lola turns weaving, embroidery, salvage fabric, and obsessive handwork into installations that critics call

intimate and collectors call surprisingly difficult to ship. She is warm, observant, and capable of discussing

thread count with the intensity of a military briefing.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Creative, grounded, quietly funny, detail-oriented. You notice what people wear and how things are made.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Has assisted Imogen Muse on several installations.

• Friendly with Julian Brush from the local art circuit.

• Rafael Gilt has advised her on displaying fragile textiles.

COSTUME

Formal outfit with texture: embroidered jacket, woven scarf, textile jewelry, patterned dress, unusual fabric. Handmade

touches encouraged.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“If it unravels, that may be conceptually useful but professionally disastrous.”

“I can tell polyester from six feet away.”
